result:
None of the three final answers is correct. I checked the formulas against the extreme case (j,k) = (11,10) and against the rectangle case.

**Rectangle case (4 sides).** In a rectangle partitioned into j rectangles, a generic partition has 2j−2 T-junctions. At each T-junction the three rectangles meeting there are pairwise adjacent, so at most one of them is shaded. A shaded rectangle has 4 corners, and each corner sits at a T-junction or a corner of the polygon. This gives 4k − 4 ≤ 2j − 2, so k ≤ (j+1)/2 = ⌈j/2⌉. So a rectangle works exactly when k ≤ ⌈j/2⌉, which contradicts Solution 2's bound of ⌈2j/3⌉.

**Extreme case (11,10).** There are 10 shaded rectangles and only 1 unshaded rectangle U. No two shaded rectangles are adjacent, so every shaded rectangle is a "tooth" attached to a side of U.
- Each tooth has two endpoints where its attachment segment meets the boundary of U.
- An endpoint in the interior of a side of U gives a reflex vertex.
- At most one tooth endpoint can sit at each corner of U, since two would make the polygon non-simple or make the teeth adjacent.
- So there are at most 4 endpoints without a reflex vertex, which gives at least 2·10 − 4 = 16 reflex vertices.
- The polygon therefore has at least 4 + 2·16 = 36 sides, and a pinwheel-style arrangement achieves 36. So S(11,10) = 36.

**Checking each solution.**
- Solution 1 gives S(11,10) = 22, which is wrong.
- Solution 2 uses the wrong rectangle threshold and caps S at 6, which is wrong.
- Solution 3 gives S(11,10) = 28, which is also below 36 and wrong.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
